analyst.summary: Central Bank of India is a government-owned public-sector bank whose asset quality has improved substantially over the past two years, alongside a healthy capital-adequacy ratio and a deep-value valuation (trading below book value with an attractive dividend yield). A large capital raise is planned, which will dilute existing shareholders somewhat, and one recent quarter's profit came in notably lower than the rest without a confirmed explanation. On balance we rate this a Hold, given the genuinely improving credit trend and cheap valuation outweigh the near-term dilution and data gaps.
